subject: computer_applications
instructions: Section A is compulsory. Attempt any four questions from Section B. Answers are written on separate paper; the first 15 minutes are for reading the paper. Section B answers are Java programs (BlueJ or any Java environment) with variable descriptions/mnemonic codes; flowcharts and algorithms are not required.

sections.name: Section A
sections.rule: Attempt all questions from this Section.

sections.name: Section B
sections.rule: Attempt any four questions from this Section.

questions.question: Character class methods are found in the package called:
questions.solution: (b) java.lang. Character is a wrapper class in java.lang, which is imported by default.

concepts: char promoted to int in arithmetic
questions.question: System.out.println('Z' + 32); will display:
questions.solution: (c) 122. 'Z' is promoted to its code 90; 90 + 32 = 122 is printed as an int.

questions.topic: Memory occupied by a double array
questions.question: double x[] = {2.5, 4.5, 5.5, 6.4}; occupies __________ bytes.
questions.solution: (d) 32. 4 elements × 8 bytes per double = 32 bytes.

concepts: / and % have equal precedence, left to right
questions.question: The output of 42/6%2 is:
questions.solution: (a) 1. 42/6 = 7, then 7 % 2 = 1 (left-to-right evaluation).

questions.topic: Index of an element in a 2D array
concepts: row and column indices start at 0
questions.question:
Consider the Two dimensional array P[2][3] of peripherals (input / output devices) given below, state the index of the device Barcode Scanner.
Row 0: Mouse | Keyboard | Printer
Row 1: Scanner | Barcode Scanner | Microphone
questions.solution: (a) P[1][1]. Barcode Scanner is in the second row (index 1) and second column (index 1).

concepts: array and class are non-primitive/user-defined types
questions.question:
Which of the following is user defined data type?
1. array
2. double
3. class
4. boolean
questions.solution: (b) 1 and 3. array and class are composite (user-defined) types; double and boolean are primitive.

concepts: loop variable skipping the terminating value
questions.question: Select the infinite loop:
questions.solution: (b) for(int i=2; i!=0;i-=3). i takes 2, -1, -4, ... and never equals 0, so i != 0 is always true.

questions.chapter: Class as the Basis of Computation
questions.question:
Which of the following is true for the given object creation statement?
Game cricket = new Game();

options.a: Game is an object of cricket class
options.c: Game is a class and cricket is an object

questions.solution: (c) Game is a class and cricket is an object. Game is the class and cricket is the object created with new.

concepts: public access is open to all
questions.question: Post office is an example for __________ access specifier.
questions.solution: (a) public. A post office can be used by everyone, just as public members are accessible from anywhere.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In switch case break statement avoids fall through.
Reason (R): break statement helps to execute only one case at a time.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is a correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is a correct explanation of (A).. break transfers control out of the switch after the matching case, which is exactly why fall through is avoided.

concepts: for loop for a fixed number of repetitions
questions.question:
A physical education teacher asks the students to do the side stretch as shown below, 10 times. Which programming construct the teacher uses?
[Picture: a figure doing a side stretch, labelled "Side Stretch" with a circular arrow and the number 10.]
questions.solution: (c) for. A task repeated a fixed number of times (10) is done with a for loop.

concepts: length is a property of arrays
questions.question: The index (subscript) of the last element of an array ar[] is
questions.solution: (d) ar.length-1. Array indices run from 0 to ar.length - 1; length is a property, not a method.

concepts: inner loop completes for each outer iteration
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A clock is a real-life example of nested loops.
Reason (R): The hour hand moves through 12 positions, while the minute hand moves through 60 positions within each hour.

options.a: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is a correct explanation of (A).
options.b: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is a correct explanation of (A).. For every position of the hour hand (outer loop), the minute hand completes all 60 positions (inner loop), which explains the assertion.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of methods will cause a compile-time error due to incorrect method overloading?

options.a: void test(int a, int b) and void test(double a, double b)
options.b: void test(int a, double b) and void test(double a, int b)
options.c: void test(int a, double b) and void test(int a)
options.d: void test(int a) and int test(int a)

questions.solution: (d) void test(int a) and int test(int a). The two methods have the same parameter list and differ only in return type, which is not valid overloading.

questions.question: Which of the following converts "25" to 25.0?
questions.solution: (c) Double.parseDouble("25"). Double.parseDouble takes a String argument and returns a double.

concepts: semicolon after for makes an empty body
questions.solution: (d) 00. The semicolon ends the loop; p goes 4, 2, 0 and the loop stops at 0. print and println then print 0 twice on the same line: 00.

concepts: compareTo returns difference of first mismatching characters
questions.question:
What is the output of the statement given below?
"ANGER".compareTo("ANGEL")
questions.solution: (c) 6. First difference is at index 4: 'R' (82) − 'L' (76) = 6.

questions.question:
Consider the following program segment in which the statements are jumbled. Choose the correct order of statements to calculate and return the factorial of 4.
for (k=1; k<=4; k++) → 1
return fa; → 2
long fa=1, k; → 3
fa*=k; → 4
questions.solution: (b) 3, 1, 4, 2. Declare/initialise (3), loop (1), multiply inside the loop (4), then return (2).

questions.question: Write the java expression to find the product of square root of P and the square root of Q using the methods of Math class.
questions.solution: Math.sqrt(P) * Math.sqrt(Q)

questions.topic: Accessing array elements; largest element index
questions.question:
Consider the following array and answer the questions given below:
int a[] = {12, 10, 8, 4, 6, 2, 3, 5, 7};
(a) What is the output of System.out.print(a[0]+a[5]);?

questions.solution:
(a) a[0] = 12, a[5] = 2, so the output is 14.
(b) The largest element is 12, at index 0.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Class as the Basis of Computation
questions.topic: Class with accept, calculate and display: slab-based cloud storage bill
concepts: class with member variables and methods
questions.question:
Define a class named CloudStorage with the following specifications:
Member Variables:
int acno – stores the user's account number.
int space – stores the amount of storage space in GB purchased by the user.
double bill – stores the total price to be paid by the user.
Member Methods:
void accept() – prompts the user to input their account number and storage space using Scanner class methods only.
void calculate() – calculates the bill total price based on the storage space purchased using the pricing table provided:
Storage range | Price per GB (Rs)
First 15 GB | 15
Next 15 GB | 13
Above 30 GB | 11
void display() – displays the account number, storage space and bill to be paid.
Write a main method to create an object of the class and invoke the methods of the class with respect to the object.

marking_points.point: Class declaration and member variables with correct data types
accept() using Scanner for acno and space
display() prints acno, space and bill
main() creates object and invokes methods in order

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Define a class to accept values into a 4 × 4 integer array. Calculate and print the NORM of the array.
NORM is the square root of sum of squares of all elements.
Example array:
1 2 1 3
5 2 1 6
3 6 1 2
3 4 6 3
Sum of squares of elements = 1 + 4 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 4 + 1 + 36 + 9 + 36 + 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 36 + 9 = 201
NORM = Square root of 201 = 14.177446878757825

marking_points.point: Class, main() and declaration of 4x4 array
Input of 16 elements using nested loops
Sum of squares of all elements
